title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2611.13358v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The extensive adoption of AI has precipitated a crisis in academic integrity. While studies attempt to quantify cheating, less is known about the motivations instructors believe students have for using AI in prohibited ways. We analyze 2.01 million posts on r/Professors to understand how instructors perceive students' justifications for AI-mediated cheating. Our qualitative analyses reveal four primary themes: (1) Academic System Gaming, (2) Digital-Academic Literacy Gap, (3) Performance Anxiety, and (4) Normalization of Dishonesty.

translated_title: 理解学生AI辅助作弊的理由：基于在线论坛分析的教师视角
translated_abstract: 人工智能的广泛采用引发了学术诚信危机。虽然已有研究试图对作弊行为进行量化，但关于教师认为学生违规使用AI的动机，目前所知甚少。我们分析了Reddit上r/Professors社区的201万条帖子，以了解教师如何认知学生对AI辅助作弊的辩护理由。我们的定性分析揭示了四个主要主题：(1) 学术系统博弈，(2) 数字-学术素养差距，(3) 表现焦虑，以及 (4) 不诚信行为的正常化。
tldr: 该研究通过分析r/Professors论坛上201万条帖子，从教师视角首次大规模揭示了学生AI作弊背后的四大动机：博弈学术系统、数字-学术素养差距、表现焦虑以及不诚信行为的正常化。
en_tdlr: This study analyzes 2.01 million posts from the r/Professors forum to reveal instructors' perceptions of four primary rationales for AI-mediated cheating: academic system gaming, digital-academic literacy gap, performance anxiety, and the normalization of dishonesty.
